Summary:

---

**Is dev-mode in parity with the current form?**

- **Yes.** Dev-mode is still aligned with the current app:
  - **http://localhost:3000/dev-mode** loads the main app at `/` in an iframe, so you always see the current UI.
  - The HUD still has **“SCAN & COPY”**, which runs the same scan (finds includeable elements, overlays, exports JSON for design/warden). So the “scans to help you build” are still there.

- **Parity check was failing** because the script was treating **`app/dist/`** (Vite build output) as a main “page.” That folder is build output, not a source page to mirror in dev-mode. The parity script now **ignores the `dist` directory**, so it only checks source pages. With that change, **parity passes** (1 main page ↔ 1 dev-mode page).

**What I changed**

- In **`scripts/check_dev_mode_parity.js`**, the main-app walk now skips the **`dist`** directory (same idea as skipping `dev-mode`), so build output is not required to have a dev-mode mirror.

**Quick reference**

- **Dev-mode URL:** `http://localhost:3000/dev-mode` (with dev server running).
- **Scans:** Use “SCAN & COPY” in the dev-mode HUD, or run `node scripts/scan.js --all` (and related flags) to scan discovered `app/dev-mode/*.html` routes.
- **Parity:** Run `npm run check:devmode:parity` (or `node scripts/check_dev_mode_parity.js`) to ensure every main source page has a dev-mode mirror; it now correctly ignores `app/dist/`.

Summary of what was done and what dev-mode does:

---

## 1. Reconciled dev-mode with main (Vite)

- **Dev-mode is the mirror of the main Vite app**: the iframe at `/dev-mode` loads the same app as `/` (the Vite app). It was not a separate HTML app; it was always a shell that embeds main. That’s unchanged and correct.
- **Updates made so dev-mode stays in sync with main:**
  - **`app/dev-mode/index.html`**  
    - Viewport and meta aligned with main: `maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no`, `theme-color`, `apple-mobile-web-app-capable`, `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style`.  
    - Comment at the top stating it’s the dev mirror of the Vite app and that the overlay provides scan/telemetry for design parity and `scripts/scan.js`.  
    - Iframe uses `data-initial-src="/"`; the overlay sets the real `src` so it works with a non-root base path.
  - **`app/dev-mode/dev-mode-overlay.js`**  
    - **Base-path aware**: `getAppBase()` derives the app base from the current URL (e.g. `/` or `/resuscitation_health_app/`). The iframe `src` is set with `resolveAbsolutePath(targetSpec.targetPath)` so it works with Vite’s `base` (e.g. GitHub Pages).  
    - **Vite detection**: `detectFramework(doc)` checks the iframe document for a module script with `/src/` or `/assets/` and sets scan meta `project.framework` to `'vite'` (otherwise `'static-html-devmode'`).
  - **Vite build**  
    - Dev-mode is part of the build: `build.rollupOptions.input` includes `'dev-mode/index.html'`, so `dist/` gets `dev-mode/index.html`.  
    - The overlay is copied into the build: the `copy-static-assets` plugin also copies `dev-mode/dev-mode-overlay.js` into `dist/dev-mode/`, so the built app can serve `/dev-mode` and the scan/overlay still work.

So dev-mode is reconciled with main (same app in iframe, same meta/viewport, base-path and build support), and it keeps its dev-mode features.

---

## 2. What dev-mode does (reference)

| Feature | What it does |
|--------|----------------|
| **URL** | `http://localhost:3000/dev-mode` (or `{base}/dev-mode` in production). |
| **Preview** | Iframe loads the **main app** at `?target=` (default `/`). So you always see the current Vite app. |
| **Query params** | `?target=/path` – path loaded in the iframe. `?algo=filename.json` – passed through so the main app can load that algorithm. |
| **Live overlay** | Green/colored boxes over the iframe content: semantic elements (header, main, div, button, etc.) with depth and label. Updates on scroll, resize, and DOM changes (MutationObserver). |
| **SCAN & COPY** | Runs the same “design telemetry” scan as the headless pipeline: geometry, typography, contrast/WCAG, layout, etc. Copies the JSON to the clipboard and exposes `window.__DEV_MODE_LAST_SCAN_JSON` and `__DEV_MODE_LAST_SCAN_META`. |
| **Headless scan** | `scripts/scan.js` opens `/dev-mode`, then calls `window.__DEV_MODE_EXPORT_SCAN(maxElements)` in the page context to get the same JSON. So scans used for design/warden runs are from the **same** Vite app you see in the iframe. |
| **Parity** | `scripts/check_dev_mode_parity.js` ensures every main **source** page has a dev-mode mirror (and we exclude `dist` so build output isn’t required to have a mirror). |

So: **main** is the Vite app (what users see). **Dev-mode** is a thin shell that embeds main in an iframe and adds the overlay + scan/export so you can run scans and design tooling against the current app. It’s now aligned with main (meta, base path, Vite detection) and included in the Vite build so it isn’t left behind.
